title: Dielectric Relaxation, Water Sorption Thermodynamics, and Humidity‐Sensing Mechanisms of Compressed Ulva Biomass Pellets
content:
This study investigates the moisture sorption thermodynamics, dielectric relaxation behavior, and humidity-sensing performance of compressed Ulva biomass pellets. The findings demonstrate that sustainable macroalgal pellets provide low hysteresis (~1.63%) and wide-range sensitivity for green environmental diagnostics.


ABSTRACT

This study investigates the moisture sorption thermodynamics, dielectric relaxation behavior, and humidity-sensing performance of compressed Ulva powder pellets prepared from Ulva sp. macroalgal biomass harvested from Abu-Qir Bay, Alexandria, Egypt. Gravimetric sorption isotherms at 25°C exhibited a sigmoidal profile well-described by the Guggenheim−Anderson−de Boer (GAB) model, yielding a monolayer moisture capacity (M 0) of 14.94%. Frequency-dependent dielectric and complex impedance measurements across a relative humidity (RH) range of 11.3%−97.3% demonstrated that moisture sorption leads to a substantial increase in permittivity and a multi-order-of-magnitude reduction in electrical impedance. Fitting the real permittivity spectra to the Debye formulation revealed a systematic increase in static permittivity (ε s) and a decrease in relaxation time (τ) with rising hydration. Generalized Cole−Cole modeling captured non-Debye relaxation behavior, supporting the interpretation that the electrical response reflects moisture-induced dipole reorientation and apparent ionic transport within the polysaccharide matrix. The compressed Ulva powder pellets demonstrated favorable humidity-sensing characteristics, including a low maximum hysteresis error (~1.63%), complemented by rapid, symmetric transient response (t90) and recovery (tre) kinetics. These quantitative findings establish a foundation for utilizing sustainable compressed Ulva biomass pellets as functional transducing elements in environmental humidity monitoring.
